verses.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸੇ ਕੁਲਾ ਬਧੂ ਗੁਰ ਜਨ ਮੈ ਘੂਘਟ ਪਟ ਸਿਹਜਾ ਸੰਜੋਗ ਸਮੈ ਅੰਤਰੁ ਨ ਪੀਅ ਸੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaise kulaa badhoo gur jan mai ghooghaT paT sihajaa sa(n)jog samai a(n)tar na peea sai ||

en.bdb: Just as a daughter-in-law covers herself with veil in front of the elders of the house, but keeps no distance from her husband at the time of sharing his bed;

verses.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸੇ ਮਣਿ ਅਛਤ ਕੁਟੰਬ ਹੀ ਸਹਿਤ ਅਹਿ ਬੰਕ ਤਨ ਸੂਧੋ ਬਿਲ ਪੈਸਤ ਹੁਇ ਜੀਅ ਸੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaise man achhat kuTa(n)b hee sahit eh ba(n)k tan soodho bil paisat hui jeea sai ||

en.bdb: Just as a snake remains crooked when with female snake and his family, but becomes straight when it enters in the burrow;

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਾਤ ਪਿਤਾ ਅਛਤ ਨ ਬੋਲੈ ਸੁਤ ਬਨਿਤਾ ਸੈ  ਪਾਛੇ ਕੈ ਦੈ ਸਰਬਸ ਮੋਹੁ ਸੁਤ ਤੀਅ ਸੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: maat pitaa achhat na bolai sut banitaa sai  paachhe kai dhai sarabas moh sut teea sai ||

en.bdb: Just as a son avoids talking to his wife in front of his parents, but when alone showers all his love upon her,

verses.gurmukhi: ਲੋਗਨ ਮੈ ਲੋਗਾਚਾਰ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਏਕੰਕਾਰ ਸਬਦ ਸੁਰਤਿ ਉਨਮਨ ਮਨ ਹੀਅ ਸੈ ॥੪੧॥
verses.translit_en: logan mai logaachaar gurmukh eka(n)kaar sabadh surat unaman man heea sai ||41||

en.bdb: Similarly a devoted Sikh appears worldly among others but having attached his mind with Guru's word, he rises spiritually and realises the Lord. Quintessence: One may maintain oneself as a worldly person outwardly but inwardly one keeps oneself attached with Naam and attains divine bliss. (41)
